Problem description:
There is a set of locations, each of which may be opened as a service facility.
The travel distance between every ordered pair of locations is given (as pairs).
Every location must be assigned to exactly one opened facility.

Decision variables:
- Select a fixed number of locations to open as facilities (the required number is specified in the input).
- Assign every location to exactly one opened facility.

Constraints:
- Each location must be assigned to exactly one facility.
- Assignments can only be made to facilities that are opened.

Objective:
Minimize the total service cost, defined as the sum of travel distances from each location to the facility that serves it.

You will receive the problem instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Your task is to choose facility locations and assignments that minimize the total travel distance over all locations.

Reply using exactly the following JSON structure (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": {
    "selected": [<location_to_open>, <location_to_open>, ...],
    "assignments": [<chosen_open_location>, <chosen_open_location>, ...]
  }
}
```
Here, `selected` is the list of locations chosen to host service centers.
The `assignments` list has the same length and order as the locations described in the input; the i-th entry specifies which opened location serves location i.
All identifiers must match exactly those used in the input, and every assignment must refer to one of the locations listed in `selected`.
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of clearings the parks department must open as dog play areas. The solution must open exactly this many sites.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for each location (candidate clearings / neighborhood parks). Use these ids to reference locations when specifying distances and assignments.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the source location in a pairwise distance record — interpreted as the neighborhood park whose travel to a candidate play area is being measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the target location in a pairwise distance record — interpreted as the candidate clearing (potential dog play area) that the source park could be assigned to.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The numeric travel distance from the source park to the target clearing (e.g., walking distance). This value is used to compute the total summed walking distance when assigning each park to an opened play area.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of candidate locations in the town (each identifier represents a city block or a potential water refill site). This tells the solver how many location identifiers appear in the instance.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of water refill stations the company is allowed to open. The solver must select this many sites from the candidate locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of all location identifiers used in this scenario. Each identifier corresponds to a block or potential station site and will be referenced by the pairwise distance entries; every listed location must be assigned to one activated station.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the origin location in a pairwise distance entry (a block or potential site). This is one end of the travel path used to compute assignment cost.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the destination location in a pairwise distance entry (a block or potential site). Distances are defined between these identifiers to evaluate travel from origin to destination.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance from the origin location to the destination location in the same row. This nonnegative value represents the cost (e.g., distance or travel time) used when summing assignment distances for the plan; units are consistent across the instance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations included in the instance — i.e., the count of entrance zones and proposed stroller-kiosk sites whose identifiers appear in the map.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many stroller rental kiosks the mall manager must open (the fixed p value). Exactly this many candidate sites will be selected as open kiosks.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of all location identifiers used in this scenario. Each identifier denotes a mall entrance area or a proposed kiosk site that must be considered for assignment to an open kiosk.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin location for this distance entry — typically an entrance area (or a location acting as a demand node) from which shoppers walk to a kiosk.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location for this distance entry — a candidate kiosk site to which the origin location could be assigned.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The walking distance between the origin and destination locations (e.g., meters or minutes). In the solution each entrance's distance to its assigned open kiosk is summed to form the objective to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of locations in the instance — i.e., the count of neighborhood points / candidate stall sites considered. This is the size of the set from which pop-up stalls may be opened and to which every neighborhood will be assigned.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many pop-up stalls must be opened. The planner must choose exactly this many candidate locations to host stalls.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for every location (each neighborhood and candidate stall site) used in the instance. Each identifier is referenced when choosing stall sites and when assigning neighborhoods to an opened stall.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source location for this pairwise entry — the neighborhood (or candidate site) from which travel to another location is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target location for this pairwise entry — the candidate stall site (or neighborhood) being measured as the destination from the origin.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance (e.g., kilometers or minutes) from the origin location to the destination location. This value is used to compute the total travel cost when assigning neighborhoods to opened stalls.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of candidate sites and residential blocks in the instance; every entry in the locations list (both potential drop‑off sites and blocks to be assigned) is included in this number.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of recycling drop‑off centers you must open from the candidate locations; exactly this many sites will be selected as open service points.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for every location in town (residential blocks and potential drop‑off sites); these IDs are referenced when specifying distances and when assigning each block to an open center.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin location for this distance entry (a residential block or a potential drop‑off site); used together with to_id to identify the pair whose travel distance is given.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location for this distance entry (a residential block or a potential drop‑off site); paired with from_id to denote the two locations between which the travel distance is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance (walking or driving) between the two named locations; these distances are used to compute the cost of assigning each residential block to an opened drop‑off center and to evaluate total system travel.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct places in the instance (every plaza and every district included). Use this to size matrices or loops over all location identifiers.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of wellness check tents the organizer must open (i.e., how many plazas will be selected as active service points).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The ordered list of all location identifiers (labels for plazas and districts). These IDs are the names used in distance pairs and when assigning each district to a chosen plaza.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin location in a distance entry — typically the district (or any node) whose travel to a candidate plaza is being measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location in a distance entry — typically the candidate plaza (tent site) that a district could be assigned to.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance from the origin to the destination in this pair. This value represents the attendee travel burden used to compute total travel when districts are assigned to opened tents (units as provided).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate sidewalk locations in the neighborhood (the number of location identifiers you can pick kiosks from and that must be assigned to an opened kiosk).

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of information kiosks you must open (the fixed count of sidewalk locations to choose as kiosks).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for each candidate sidewalk location. Each identifier names a spot that can host a kiosk and that must be assigned to one opened kiosk for computing walking distances.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the sidewalk location being served (the origin of a walk). Used as the source location that would walk to a kiosk at the destination location when computing assignment cost.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the candidate sidewalk location that could host a kiosk (the destination). Assignments to an opened kiosk at this destination use the distance given here.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The walking distance from the origin sidewalk to the destination sidewalk (along pedestrian routes). This value is the cost added to the total objective if the origin is assigned to a kiosk at the destination.
